sources.title: NSDA Nationals 2023 World Schools Debate Final Round
WSDC 2025 Grand Final — India v Australia

metadata.reportedResult: India Proposition, reported 9-0 but tab not independently verified

insight.motion: This House supports a people's democratic right to secede
insight.argument: Democratic consent cannot be perpetual; political legitimacy requires a meaningful ability to revoke consent.
insight.weighing: Frames the right as a prior legitimacy question rather than a guarantee that every exercise is optimal.
qualityNotes: Candidate threshold framing; verify against captions before approval.

insight.motion: This House supports a people's democratic right to secede
insight.mechanism: A credible secession threat can force devolution and shift negotiations toward autonomy even if separation does not occur.
qualityNotes: Candidate fallback-solvency mechanism; verify before approval.

insight.motion: This House supports a people's democratic right to secede

insight.motion: This House supports a people's democratic right to secede
